gap: No result ChatGPT got says that a typical 120 V-only portable generator can't charge any of the 24 V low-frequency split-phase inverter-chargers it recommends (Sun Gold LF 6000 W and 4000 W, AIMS, Sigineer). Each maker says the AC input needs 240 V. Sun Gold says the unit 'requires 240VAC input', and Sigineer lists a charger input range of 160–264 Vac, so 120 V is below the minimum.
standout_why: Pages compared: the cited Sigineer APC6024D page, ecosolarkits' split-phase guide, liveoffthegrid's spec table and dealectric's own page. The cited Sigineer page gives the 240 Vac nominal and 160–264 Vac input range but never says what that means for a 120 V generator. Ecosolarkits says 'needs a 240V AC input (not 120V)' only for a 48 V Sungold 15,000 W unit and names no 24 V split-phase model ('sold out'). Liveoffthegrid has a 'Gen in' yes/no column, covers no 24 V models and says nothing about 120 V generators. Our page covers no 24 V models and does not discuss AC or generator input. So rivals have part of the fact (the 240 V input spec) but none spells out the 120 V generator exclusion for the 24 V picks.
decides: This doesn't change which inverter is best. It sets a buying condition for all ChatGPT's 24 V picks: the shopper needs grid power, a 120/240 V generator, or a 240 V-capable generator to charge or pass power through. A buyer with only a 120 V inverter generator gets no AC charging from any of these LF units, according to the makers' stated input specs. Per leg, the cited Sigineer APC6024D page already gives 3,000 W per 120 V leg, so a 6,000 W unit is 3,000 W on one leg.

Sun Gold 6000 W / 4000 W 24 V LF: I looked for the per-leg 120 V rating, the list of battery-type settings including any LiFePO4 position, and the UL status. The product page returned HTTP 429 on three tries and the store search snippet didn't include them.

Sigineer High Power Inverter Charger manual PDF: I downloaded it to check for any 120 V-input wiring option or jumper. The PDF has no text layer for WebFetch, and running pdftotext locally needed approval I didn't have.
WZRELB 4000W 24V (Walmart card, $467.10): I found no maker page or manual for its AC input, certification or per-leg limit and didn't research it further.

Whether any of these LF units can charge from a 120 V-only generator through a setting or jumper: no maker document found. The only such report is a DIY Solar Forum user about a different model (Sun Gold SPH6548P, setting #68), which I didn't use.
